summary: Jordan’s ecosystem pledges are entirely restoration-focused: 32,500 urban trees, 2 million forest-tree plantings, 200,000 dunums of rangeland restoration, and an additional 1,000 dunums for combined afforestation and rangeland restoration. A supporting passage separately reports 1 million afforested trees and around 11,900 tons of CO₂-equivalent sequestration each year from these nature-based measures. The repeated urban-tree figure is counted once. These efforts address a landscape where bare land covers 90.9% of Jordan, while mapped forest and grassland cover only 25 km² and 16 km², respectively. Because no tree-density or dunum-to-km² conversion is supplied, the targets cannot be compared directly with those class areas; none of the restoration targets has a stated deadline.

targets.context: Settlement covers 633 km² (0.7%); no plantation density is supplied to express the target as an area share.

The combined area is not allocated between the mapped forest (25 km²) and grassland (16 km²) classes.
